Remove list and enumeration markers from text

Source: R/corpus.R
strip_list_markers.Rd

strip_list_markers() removes the markers of numbered and lettered lists, such as "1.", "(ii)", "(a)" and "IV.", from the text itself, before segmentation and encoding. Such markers, common in texts taken from documents, forms, or reports, carry no meaning, but they split sentences where there is no sentence boundary, shift the embeddings, and appear in the representative texts.

It removes a one- or two-digit number with a period where a list can be (at the start of the text or of a sentence, or continuing a list); a parenthesized number, single letter, or Roman numeral; and an upper-case Roman numeral with a period. A marker must stand alone, so a number that ends a sentence ("in the top 20."), years, decimals, and words in parentheses are kept. The result is text with the markers removed and white space collapsed.

The numbers, roman_numerals, and section_numbers arguments of topics() filter the terms only. clean_corpus() applies this function together with other cleaning steps.

Usage

strip_list_markers(text)

Arguments

text

A character vector without missing values.

Value

text with the markers removed, runs of white space collapsed to one space, and each element trimmed.

See also

clean_corpus(), which includes this step; dedupe(); segment().

Examples

strip_list_markers(c("1. background 2. methods", "(i) first (ii) second"))
#> [1] "background methods" "first second"      
strip_list_markers("the concept of (civil) society in (2020)")
#> [1] "the concept of (civil) society in (2020)"
strip_list_markers("The student ranks in the top 20. Good work.")
#> [1] "The student ranks in the top 20. Good work."
